summary: Denmark follows Schengen area rules. EU nationals can travel there with a valid passport or a national identity card. Nationals of the countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries listed in Annex I need a visa; the Visa Code sets the visa fee at EUR 90. ETIAS is not yet in operation. The Danish Immigration Service says a visa to enter Denmark or another Schengen country is not valid for entry into the Faroe Islands or Greenland.

Denmark's citizen portal borger.dk says visitors whose licence is from another country and not written in Latin letters must carry either an international driving licence or a translation into Danish, English or French, made by a public authority or an organisation authorised to do so in the issuing country. Licences from the Faroe Islands, Greenland, Switzerland and EU/EEA countries can be used as they are. The UK government says a UK photocard driving licence can be used to drive in Denmark, and Canada's travel advice says Canadians should carry an international driving permit. driving.text: Denmark is a party to the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). Denmark's citizen portal borger.dk says visitors whose licence is from another country and not written in Latin letters must carry either an international driving licence or a translation into Danish, English or French, made by a public authority or an organisation authorised to do so in the issuing country. Licences from the Faroe Islands, Greenland, Switzerland and EU/EEA countries can be used as they are. The UK government says a UK photocard driving licence can be used to drive in Denmark, and Canada's travel advice says Canadians should carry an international driving permit. No official source we could read states for how long a visitor may drive on a foreign licence. Denmark's Road Traffic Act (§ 53) makes it drink-driving to drive a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration above 0.50 per mille; for an ordinary car (category B) the limit is 0.20 per mille within the first 3 years after the driver first obtained the right to drive one.

tips.text: The Danish Immigration Service says a visa to enter Denmark or another Schengen country is not valid for entry into the Faroe Islands or Greenland: travellers from a country with a visa requirement need a visa sticker that states it is valid for entry to the Faroe Islands and/or Greenland.

The Danish Immigration Service says visa-free travellers may stay in the Schengen region, Greenland and the Faroe Islands for a maximum combined of 90 days in any 180-day period, and that citizens of Australia, Canada, Chile, Israel, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea and the US are entitled to stay in Denmark for 90 days or 3 months regardless of stays in other Schengen countries.

The UK Foreign Office and Canada say cyclists often have the right of way in Denmark: drivers should check cycle lanes before turning right, and pedestrians should watch carefully for bicycles when crossing.
The official ETIAS website, travel-europe.europa.eu, says ETIAS will cost EUR 20.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Denmark?
faq.answer: EU nationals can travel to Denmark with a valid passport or a national identity card, and the EU–Switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons lets Swiss nationals enter simply upon production of a valid identity card or passport. Nationals of the countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. Nationals of the countries listed in Annex I need a visa; the Visa Code sets the visa fee at EUR 90.

faq.question: Does a Schengen visa cover the Faroe Islands and Greenland?
faq.answer: No. The Danish Immigration Service says a visa to enter Denmark or another Schengen country is not valid for entry into the Faroe Islands or Greenland. Travellers from a country with a visa requirement must have a visa that is valid for entry into the Faroe Islands and/or Greenland, and the visa sticker must state it. The UK Foreign Office says Greenland and the Faroe Islands are not members of the EU.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Denmark?
faq.answer: ETIAS is the new travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers to enter 30 European countries, Denmark among them. It is not yet in operation and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official ETIAS website lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: Does Denmark use the euro?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says the currency of Denmark is the Danish krone (DKK), and that some stores add a surcharge when you pay with a foreign credit card.

faq.question: How do I stay in Denmark longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office tells British nationals that to stay longer than 90 days in a 180-day period they must meet the Danish government's entry requirements, and that time in Denmark with a residence permit or long-stay visa does not count towards the 90-day visa-free limit.
